taxonomyNote: NatureServe treats V. macrotis as separate from V. velox.
fieldMarks: Smallest canid in North America, 1.6-2.7 kg
Exceptionally large ears (71-95 mm) set close together
Yellowish to gray coat with a darker back and light underside and inner ears
Distinct dark patches on each side of the nose and at the tail tip
behavior: Spends most of its time in dens, which it digs or takes over from prairie dogs, other rodents and badgers
Barks at perceived threats; uses a hacking growl with other foxes
Main prey is the most abundant nocturnal rodent or lagomorph locally
habitat: Open desert, shrubby or shrub-grass habitat, at 400-1,900 m; also chaparral, valley grassland and some agricultural and urban areas.
range: Southeastern Oregon, Nevada, Utah, western Colorado, southern California, Arizona, New Mexico and western Texas, south to central Mexico.

lookalikes.name: Swift fox
lookalikes.howToTell: Smaller ears, broader snout, shorter tail; Great Plains range.
